case.title: BTR's Tangier anode plant
case.subtitle: BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology · Tanger Tech City, Morocco
case.question: Can Sayari show who owns BTR's new Moroccan anode plant, and whether it already ships graphite to the US?
case.headline: The reverse of Case 1: ownership is visible, and trade has only just begun. Sayari traces BTR's Moroccan subsidiary to BTR in China through a Singapore holding company, 100% at each step. In Aug 2026 the plant received its first artificial graphite (1,240 t) from BTR's own Indonesian plant, and it has exported nothing yet. The 3,088 'graphite' shipments from Morocco to the US are mostly mislabelled fertilizers and chemicals, plus a little European industrial graphite.
case.summary_for_non_experts: BTR, the world's biggest maker of graphite for battery anodes, is building a 60,000-tonne-a-year anode plant near Tangier through a local subsidiary. Morocco has a US free-trade agreement, so a plant there could one day supply US battery makers. Sayari's company records show that the plant belongs to BTR, via Singapore and a BTR subsidiary in Jiangsu. So far the plant has only imported building materials and machinery from China. None of the large Morocco-to-US 'graphite' trade is battery material.

steps.title: The plant: two companies, six records
steps.text: Sayari holds two Moroccan BTR companies, registered in Oct 2023 and May 2024, and four customs-data fragments. One fragment shares the registry address (Lot 25, Tanger Tech), so we merge it as Inferred. The other three match by name only and stay leads.

steps.title: The owner: visible this time
steps.text: Moroccan records name a Singapore holding company, BNUO International, as 100% owner. Singapore records show BNUO is 100% owned by BTR (Jiangsu), and Chinese records show BTR owns all of BTR (Jiangsu). One step is a 'possibly same as' link between two BNUO records, backed by a shared officer, Yang Shunyi. BTR's own release confirms the subsidiary. The same person, Yang Shunyi, is director of the Singapore holding company and manager of the Moroccan plant company, with an address in BTR's home district of Shenzhen. One hop is a record match: the Singapore record of BTR (Jiangsu) is linked to the Chinese registry record by name and address, not by a shared identifier.

steps.title: Inputs: construction goods, then BTR graphite
steps.text: From Nov 2025 to Jun 2026, the plant's rows are construction goods from China: pipes, racks, machinery. Then, on 19 Aug 2026, three rows of artificial graphite (HS 3801.10, 1,240 t, about US$857,000) left BTR's Indonesian plant in Morowali for the Tangier anode company. That is graphite moving between two BTR-owned plants. Nothing has left Tangier yet.

steps.title: The corridor: a mislabelled bucket
steps.text: The 3,088 Morocco-to-US artificial graphite rows are led by fertilizer, pesticide and oil firms such as Haifa Negev, Coromandel, Gandhar, Rotem Amfert and ADAMA. The main buyers are in Colombia, Mexico and Ecuador. Most rows describe fertilizer bags or chemical drums, and many share the same few arrival dates. This looks like a data error, not graphite trade.

steps.title: The real graphite is industrial
steps.text: The real graphite on the route is European electrode and rod stock: SGL Carbon (France to its US arm), GrafTech (Switzerland to GrafTech USA) and one Resonac electrode to a Mexican steelmaker. Sizes are in millimetres and inches, so it is industrial grade, not anode powder. Sayari shows no Morocco-to-US shipments from BTR, Gotion, CNGR/COBCO, Hailiang or Shinzoom.

The Morocco-to-US HS 3801.10 bucket is dominated by mislabelled fertilizer, pesticide and chemical cargo for Latin American buyers. The real graphite in it is industrial (SGL Carbon, GrafTech, Resonac).

caveats: Building a plant in Morocco with Chinese ownership is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
The fertilizer, chemical and graphite companies are named because they appear in the HS 3801.10 bucket. Most appear only because of an apparent coding error in one trade data source.
We read about 90 of the 3,088 corridor rows (ranked results), not all of them. A small battery-grade flow could still be hidden in the rest.
'Departure Morocco' probably often means transshipment through Tanger Med; the European graphite rows likely did not originate in Morocco.
Entity-resolution links are our judgment and could be wrong. The Yang Shunyi match is across records with reversed name order.
Sayari free-text queries rank rows but do not filter them; counts after a quoted query are not counts of matches.
The Aug 2026 graphite rows were found in an 18 Oct 2026 re-check; they were either newer than the first search or filed under a trade record the first search missed.

Which company runs which line: a 13 Aug 2024 filing by BTR's largest shareholder (see Case 9) names 'BTR Mediterranean Anode' as the anode company. That is the Rian-owned company; the BNUO-owned one is more likely the cathode company. The ownership chain shown in step 2 is the BNUO company's. The anode company's chain runs through Rian International Holding to a Singapore record of BTR.
case.answer: Ownership: yes. Registry data shows BTR owning the Tangier company 100% through a Singapore holding company, and the same executive runs both. Shipments: inbound only so far. In Aug 2026, BTR's Indonesian plant sent 1,240 t of artificial graphite to the Tangier anode company; nothing has left the plant yet.
case.why_it_matters: Morocco has a US free-trade agreement, and BTR's plant is meant to supply Western carmakers. Because ownership is already on record, US buyers can tell the plant is Chinese-owned before its first shipment, which is exactly what the tax-credit rules ask them to check.

calls.question: Who ships artificial graphite (HS 3801.10) from Morocco to the US?
calls.result_summary: 646 suppliers, but only country buckets came back (India 261, USA 203, China 194, Spain 186...). No supplier names. Buyer countries include Colombia, Mexico, Ecuador and Guatemala, which is odd for a US-arrival filter.
calls.interpretation: The supplier-scope facet can't name shippers. Non-US buyer countries were a first hint that the bucket is not what it seems.

calls.question: What records does Sayari hold for BTR's Moroccan subsidiary?
calls.result_summary: 6 records: two registry companies in Morocco (BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology, RC 142409 with an LEI; BTR Mediterranean Anode New Material Technology, RC 149725) and four customs-data fragments with no country.
calls.interpretation: Two separate legal entities plus four trade fragments. One fragment shares the registry address (Lot 25, Tanger Tech).

calls.question: Who owns and runs BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology?
calls.result_summary: SASU registered 2023-10-09. 100% shareholder and beneficial owner: BNUO International Holding Pte. Ltd (Singapore). General manager Shunyi Yang; board member Pingzhou Yang. Trade count 0 sent, 0 received.
calls.interpretation: Unlike Case 1, the registry data names a shareholder. The registry record itself has no trade.

calls.question: Who owns BTR Mediterranean Anode New Material Technology?
calls.result_summary: Registered 2024-05-03 in Tangier. 100% shareholder: Rian International Holding Pte. Ltd (Singapore). Director Zerui Fang. No trade.
calls.interpretation: A second BTR company in Tangier, held through a different Singapore holding company.

calls.question: Does the ownership chain reach BTR in China?
calls.result_summary: 2 owners: BNUO International Holding (1 hop) and BTR New Material Group (jeHf5QJt0JXowTiCA8JiIQ) at path length 4, via a 'possibly same as' Singapore registry record of BNUO.
calls.interpretation: Yes. BTR New Material Group is visible as the ultimate owner, with one 'possibly same as' step.

calls.question: Does the second company's chain reach BTR?
calls.result_summary: 2 owners: Rian International Holding (1 hop) and a Singapore record of 'BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd.' (UEN T23UF7645F) at path length 3, via a 'possibly same as' Rian record.
calls.interpretation: This chain also ends at BTR, but at a Singapore filing record that Sayari has not merged with the main BTR entity.

calls.question: What exactly links the Moroccan plant to BTR?
calls.result_summary: Path: BTR Mediterranean ← BNUO (Moroccan record) ~ BNUO Pte. Ltd. (Singapore registry, possibly same as) ← BTR (Jiangsu) New Material Technology ← BTR New Material Group.
calls.interpretation: An ownership path, not a trade link. Compare Case 1, where the shortest path was a shipment.

calls.question: Who is behind BNUO International Holding in Singapore?
calls.result_summary: UEN 202332562W, registered 2023-08-14, holding company at Duo Tower, Fraser Street. 100% shareholder BTR (Jiangsu). Its CEO is also general manager of the Moroccan company (an individual, named in Sayari). Also owns Envolvic International Holding. Mass-address and nominee-director flags.
calls.interpretation: The Singapore step is a corporate-services shell, but its shareholder is a BTR subsidiary. Yang Shunyi also runs the Moroccan company, which supports the 'possibly same as' link.

calls.question: Is BTR (Jiangsu) wholly owned by BTR?
calls.result_summary: BTR (Jiangsu) New Material Technology, Changzhou, USCC 91320413MA1NAU5H7M, registered 2017-01-16. 100% shareholder BTR New Material Group. Holds 100% of BNUO. Chairman Yang Shunyi.
calls.interpretation: Every step is 100%. Yang Shunyi's name appears at the Jiangsu, Singapore and Moroccan companies (a cross-script name match).

calls.question: What has the Moroccan plant shipped or received?
calls.result_summary: 10 rows, all inbound from China to Morocco, Nov 2025 – Jun 2026: racks and pipelines (Master Union Logistics, 3), steel pipes (Shenzhen Haizhuolian Energy, 4), machinery and unspecified goods (Sinotrans, 2), one row from China Construction Yangtze International Engineering. No graphite, no exports.
calls.interpretation: Construction-stage inputs only. The trail from this plant has not started.

calls.question: Who are the top shippers and buyers in the 3,088 Morocco-to-US HS 3801.10 rows?
calls.result_summary: 3,088 rows, all from one data source. Top suppliers by ID: Haifa Negev Technologies 302, Coromandel 147, Gandhar Oil Refinery 135, Rotem Amfert 117, ADAMA 114. Top buyers: Uniphos Colombia 111, Haifa Mexico 96, Haifa Colombia 77, Interoc 65. Earliest date bucket 2021 despite the 2024 filter.
calls.interpretation: The biggest 'graphite' shippers are fertilizer, pesticide and oil companies, and the biggest buyers are in Latin America.

calls.question: What do the corridor rows actually describe?
calls.result_summary: 50 rows read. 8 are graphite: SGL Carbon SAS → SGL Carbon LLC (graphite rods, mm sizes) and GrafTech Switzerland → GrafTech USA (artificial graphite). The other 42 are fertilizers, pesticides, acids, solvents and plastics, mostly to Latin America. 41 of the 50 arrive on just three dates (27 Jun, 29 Jun, 5 Jul 2025).
calls.interpretation: The bucket is mostly mislabelled. These look like Latin America-bound cargo moving through Tanger Med and a US transit point, all given a graphite code. Real graphite in it is industrial.

calls.question: Do any Chinese-linked battery plants in Morocco ship anything out?
calls.result_summary: 8 rows. One real hit: COBCO → Jiangmen Umicore Chang Xin (China), inorganic compounds, May 2025. The rest are false matches: timber described as '2&BTR' grade and one asphalt row.
calls.interpretation: No Gotion, CNGR, Hailiang, Shinzoom or BTR exports from Morocco to the US in Sayari.

calls.question: Is there any real graphite, battery grade or not, on this route?
calls.result_summary: Total 3,104 (the quoted phrases rank rows but don't filter them). The top 20 rows are graphite: SGL Carbon (7), GrafTech to GrafTech USA (11) and GrafTech International Holdings (1), and a Resonac Graphite Spain electrode to Grupo Acerero, Mexico (1). None mention anode material or spherical graphite. The rest are the same mislabelled chemicals.
calls.interpretation: The real graphite on the route is European industrial graphite (electrodes, rods) owned by Western and Japanese firms. Nothing battery grade.

params.query: BTR Morocco Tangier anode plant 60,000 tonnes production start 2026

calls.question: What is the plant's status, and does BTR call it a subsidiary?
calls.result_summary: BTR's own release names BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology as the subsidiary for a 60,000 t/yr anode project (up to $366m) in Tangier Tech City. CSCEC (14 Jul 2026) says it is building the factory, with production in phases from 2026. The project has two bases: 60,000 t anode and 50,000 t cathode.
calls.interpretation: The plant is under construction, which fits the construction-only imports. BTR's statement independently supports the ownership chain.

params.query: Chinese battery material plants Morocco Gotion CNGR COBCO Hailiang Shinzoom status 2026

calls.question: Which other Chinese battery-material plants in Morocco could ship graphite?
calls.result_summary: COBCO (Al Mada and CNGR) began making cathode precursor in Jorf Lasfar in June 2025. Gotion's Kenitra gigafactory targets Q3 2026. Hailiang plans copper foil. Shinzoom's parent postponed its anode project in June 2025 and ended it in June 2026 (Ecofin).
calls.interpretation: None of these is an operating graphite anode exporter, which fits finding no Chinese-owned graphite shipper on the route.

calls.question: Which people run BTR's Moroccan company?
calls.purpose: Officers linking the plant to its parent
calls.result_summary: Two people: Shunyi Yang (manager) and Pingzhou Yang (member of the board), both from Singapore-sourced records.
calls.interpretation: The Moroccan company's manager can be checked against the officers of its Singapore parent.

calls.question: Who are the directors of the Singapore holding company (BNUO)?
calls.purpose: Officers linking the plant to its parent
calls.result_summary: Seven officers. Three are local nominee or registered-agent directors flagged for mass business registration, and one is the auditor. Three directors have Chinese addresses: Yang Shunyi (Guangming District, Shenzhen, the district where BTR is headquartered), Huang Youyuan (Beijing) and Huang Aimin (Nanshan District, Shenzhen).
calls.interpretation: Yang Shunyi directs the Singapore holding company and manages the Moroccan plant company. The person links the two companies, alongside the 100% shareholding.
